ilos.text: ILO 1: Demonstrate a clear understanding of the course structure, expectations, and key programming concepts in Java, including how these skills align with real- world IT challenges and professional ethical standards. [CLO1]

original.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
original.explanation: The ILO is about this week's orientation (course structure, expectations), so it is on topic. But it has four gaps. First, "Demonstrate a clear understanding" is vague and gives no observable performance. Second, it asks for "key programming concepts in Java" and for alignment with "real- world IT challenges and professional ethical standards", and the Week 1 content (orientation, requirements, objectives, grading and policies) teaches none of these. Third, the Bloom level is too high for an orientation. Fourth, it is too broad to guide teaching or assessment.
original.targetQuote: Demonstrate a clear understanding of the course structure, expectations, and key programming concepts in Java

r2.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
r2.explanation: The ILO is partly about the orientation content (course structure, expectations), but it also asks for 'key programming concepts in Java' and how they 'align with real- world IT challenges and professional ethical standards'. The Week 1 content (course contents, requirements, objectives, grading, policies) teaches no Java concepts, no real-world IT challenges and no professional ethics. 'Demonstrate a clear understanding' is also a vague verb, not an observable performance.

original.draft: ILO 1: Describe the course structure, objectives, requirements, grading system and policies on absences, tardiness and examinations, and state what is expected of students in learning Java programming.

r2.draft: ILO 1: Explain the course structure, objectives, requirements, grading system and policies, and state their own expectations of the course. [CLO1]
r2.rawDraft: ILO 1: Explain the course structure, objectives, requirements, grading system and policies, and state their own expectations of the course. [CLO1]
r2.correctionReason: The content is a legitimate orientation, and the mismatch comes from the ILO adding Java concepts, real-world challenges and ethics that Week 1 does not teach. Revising the ILO to fit the orientation fixes this without touching the content or the week's activities and tasks. The ILO keeps its [CLO1] label.

ilos.text: ILO10: Demonstrate the Augustinian, Marian and missionary Christ- centered Spirituality through value webbing. [CLO 4]

original.label: NOT_ALIGNED
original.explanation: The source (Week 1 content) is a course orientation: course contents, requirements and activities, objectives, grading system and policies on absences, tardiness and examinations. The target ILO asks students to demonstrate Augustinian, Marian and missionary Christ-centered Spirituality through value webbing. (1) The ILO is not about this week's content: nothing in the orientation teaches or introduces spirituality or value webbing. (2) The verb 'Demonstrate' is observable, but the performance (value webbing) is not specified and nothing in the content prepares it. (3) A Demonstrating-level performance on spirituality is far above what an orientation week can teach. (4) The ILO brings in a skill, value webbing, that the content never teaches. It belongs to a later value-integration lesson or to the course CLO, not to the orientation. The ILO should be about the orientation content, such as the course objectives and requirements.
original.targetQuote: Demonstrate the Augustinian, Marian and missionary Christ- centered Spirituality through value webbing

r2.label: NOT_ALIGNED
r2.explanation: The target ILO asks students to demonstrate Augustinian, Marian and missionary Christ-centered Spirituality through value webbing. The source Week 1 content is only a course orientation (introduction to contents, requirements, objectives, grading and policies). It teaches nothing about Augustinian-Marian spirituality or value webbing, so students cannot reach the ILO from this content. Demonstrating a spirituality is also a higher-level performance than orientation content can teach. The ILO is not drawn from this week's content; and its wording is also not observable as written, because 'demonstrate spirituality' gives no concrete performance. The same ILO10 number also appears in weeks 12-14 for a different outcome, which adds to the confusion.
r2.targetQuote: Demonstrate the Augustinian, Marian and missionary Christ- centered Spirituality through value webbing.

ilos.text: ILO1: To develop skills in analysis and design of both analog and digital circuits [CLO1]
ILO2: Understand the design process of electronic circuits and systems. [CLO1]

original.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
original.explanation: The target ILO is related to the source content, but it has several gaps. (1) "To develop skills" is not an observable, assessable student performance; it names no action the student can show. (2) "both analog and digital circuits" is broader than the source content, which covers electronic systems, design of circuits and differential amplifiers (differential gain, common mode gain, CMRR, configurations) and teaches no digital circuit content. (3) The ILO names neither the differential amplifier topics nor the electronic system design topics the week actually teaches, so it is too vague to guide teaching and assessment. (4) "analysis and design" needs a stated object and expected evidence, and the history, notation and classification topics only support this at a lower level.
original.targetQuote: develop skills in analysis and design of both analog and digital circuits

r2.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
r2.explanation: The ILO (target) is about analysis and design of analog and digital circuits, and the week's content (source) covers design of electronic systems and circuits and differential amplifiers, so it is partly on topic. Gaps: (1) the ILO says "both analog and digital circuits", but the content covers only analog differential amplifiers and general system design, with no digital circuit topic; (2) "develop skills in analysis and design" is vague and gives no observable performance; (3) the content only lists topic names (Design of Electronic Circuits, Differential Gain, CMRR) and does not show circuits being analysed or designed, so the Analyze/Create level is not supported. The ILO text is also shared with Week 7-8, so changing it could affect that week; the content can be extended instead.
